answer: An identity exists only as a shard of the meadow, and a prism signs the erasure code that fixes the meadow's shard count. The kth shard under one prism must carry every earlier parity block, so it binds k ember and occupies k blocks; the prism's count is read atomically, so no batch adds two shards. A fresh prism must be countersigned by the operator's existing prism, which charges the current shard count before the new prism can issue its first shard. The bill is ember bonded per shard, rising with the shards one operator holds.
